oil.summary: Crude is stabilising after a brutal week: WTI settled at $90.98/bbl (+0.53% today) and Brent at $98.36/bbl (+0.07%), but both contracts are nursing weekly losses of roughly 12-16% after shedding more than $11/bbl from opening levels near $102 — the market's sharpest weekly decline in months. The selloff is being driven by U.S. midterm election results that raised hopes of de-escalation in the U.S.-Iran conflict, compressing the geopolitical risk premium that had underpinned crude. Asia's fuel oil margins have slumped on the same de-escalation narrative, while HPCL continues to struggle securing tankers for Hormuz transits. On the Russia side, a temporary U.S. easing of Russian oil sanctions has rattled European allies, and Russian diesel tankers that were initially tracked toward the U.S. have reportedly redirected after hitting sanctions headwinds. CME options markets price a 77% probability of an OPEC cut at the next meeting in May 2027.
drivers: U.S. midterm results fuelling de-escalation hopes for the U.S.-Iran conflict, sharply unwinding the geopolitical risk premium in crude
Temporary U.S. easing of Russia oil sanctions adding supply-side bearish pressure and straining transatlantic allied relations
Strait of Hormuz tanker disruptions persisting (HPCL unable to secure vessels), capping the downside and keeping Heating Oil spreads elevated

gas.summary: Henry Hub edged up to $2.986/MMBtu today (+1.32%), recovering modestly on the week (+3.04%) but still down nearly 6% on the month. Headline flow for the natural gas sector is relatively thin today. The Baker Hughes rig count showed a minor week-on-week uptick in U.S. oil and gas drilling activity despite the crude price crash, suggesting producers have not yet meaningfully curtailed activity. On the geopolitical supply-chain side, Hungary announced it will end Russian natural gas imports by autumn 2027, a notable longer-term demand shift for European LNG. Norway's production outlook drew attention, with reports flagging a major decline risk absent new discoveries — a potential medium-term tightener for European gas balances.
drivers: Modest daily rebound in Henry Hub (+1.32%) after a soft month, with the weekly move turning positive
Hungary committing to exit Russian gas by autumn 2027, reinforcing European LNG demand trajectory
U.S. rig count ticking slightly higher despite the oil price rout, suggesting near-term associated gas supply remains intact

power.summary: EU Carbon (EUA) fell to $82.62/EUA today (-2.78%), extending a weekly decline of 2.66%, though the one-month move remains marginally positive (+0.11%). The carbon selloff appears linked to broader energy market de-escalation sentiment following the U.S. midterms. On the structural side, two significant bullish signals emerged: European grid investment spending has surged 155% since 2019 and is expected to continue rising through 2030, per European network data; and the IEA projects 4,800 GW of new renewable capacity by 2031, explicitly citing the Strait of Hormuz crisis and fuel price spike as accelerants for the energy transition. Iran's review of 'concrete proposals' on its nuclear programme adds an additional wildcard for energy market risk sentiment.
drivers: EUA prices under pressure (-2.78%) as de-escalation hopes reduce near-term energy scarcity fears and risk premiums
European grid capex up 155% since 2019 with further increases planned through 2030, underpinning long-run power infrastructure investment thesis
IEA forecasting 4,800 GW of new renewables by 2031, with the Hormuz crisis cited as a structural accelerant for the energy transition
